result:
Review complete. I traced every phase against the v7.0 sources in `docs/sleep/ksrc/` and checked the live sysfs state (s2idle; port GPP0 at 0000:00:01.1 has `_PRW`, wakeup currently `enabled`, port/GPU/audio all runtime-suspended, GPU ACPI node not power-manageable, so the card's D3cold is the port's `_PS3`).

## Findings

**1. BLOCKING — wake policy §D defeats nvsleep: disabling `power/wakeup` on 0000:00:01.1 makes the PCI core runtime-resume the port during `dpm_suspend`, which wakes the GPU, so every idle sleep aborts with -EBUSY.**
`scripts/luminos-wake-policy:21`, interacting with `docs/sleep/ksrc/drivers_pci_pci-driver.c:844` and `drivers_pci_pci.c:2793`.
Scenario: the port is runtime-suspended with ACPI wake armed (`pci_finish_runtime_suspend` → `__pci_enable_wake` → `prepare_count=1`). `acpi_pci_need_resume()` returns true when `device_may_wakeup(port) != !!prepare_count`; after §D sets the port to `disabled`, that is true. `pci_pm_suspend(port)` then calls `pm_runtime_resume(port)` → `pci_pm_runtime_resume` → `pci_pm_bridge_power_up_actions` → `pci_resume_bus` → `pm_request_resume(GPU)` and `(audio)`. The GPU's runtime PM is still enabled in that phase, so the pm_wq worker runs a full RM runtime resume. `device_suspend_late(GPU)` then finds it active → `nv_pmops_suspend_late` → -EBUSY. Net effect: the card is woken twice per attempt, the attempt aborts, the lid supervisor retries forever, and once a retry lands inside the 500 ms autosuspend window the stock (slow) path runs. Today, with wakeup `enabled`, there is no mismatch and this path is dormant.
Fix: remove 0000:00:01.1 from `DISABLE` in `luminos-wake-policy` (leave the bridge_d3 default `enabled`; with the card off the port cannot wake the box anyway). Same mismatch will needlessly runtime-resume 00:02.2 and 00:03.1 at every suspend, but that only costs time. Also note `drivers_pci_pci.c:2793` goes through `platform_pci_need_resume`, which returns true for any bridge if `mem_sleep` is ever switched to `deep`; nvsleep only works under s2idle.
(Kernel text for `acpi_pci_need_resume` and the pcieport `DPM_FLAG_NO_DIRECT_COMPLETE|SMART_SUSPEND` flags are not in `ksrc/`; I quoted them from memory, WebFetch was not permitted. Both have been stable since 5.x.)

**2. HIGH — the live test's `MAX_GPU_RESUMES=0` will fail a correct idle run.** `tests/nvsleep/live.sh:18`, `drivers_base_power_runtime.c:793`.
pcieport has no `DPM_FLAG_MAY_SKIP_RESUME`, so `device_suspend` (`main.c:1924`) sets `must_resume=true` on the port. `device_resume_noirq(port)` → `pci_pm_resume_noirq` → `pci_pm_default_resume_early` powers the port up from D3cold → `pci_pm_bridge_power_up_actions` → `pci_resume_bus` → `pm_request_resume(0000:01:00.0)`. `trace_rpm_resume` fires before the `disable_depth` check, so an `rpm_resume: 0000:01:00.0 ... dep-1` event lands inside `dpm_resume_noirq` (exactly line 175 of the existing trace). It returns -EACCES and nothing resumes, but the test counts it. Fix: exclude events with `dep-1`, or count `nv_pmops_runtime_resume` calls instead.

**3. MEDIUM — resume-side goal only partly met; the card is physically re-powered on every resume.** `drivers_pci_pci-driver.c:998` and `:1027`.
Same chain as finding 2: the port's noirq resume powers the slot (the 0.6 s `pci_bridge_wait_for_secondary_bus` is still paid), then `pci_pm_resume(GPU)` sees `state_saved` (true since the runtime suspend) and runs `pci_restore_standard_config` (PMCSR reads D0 after the power cycle, config restored). The card sits in D0 with runtime status "suspended" until `dpm_complete` drops the port's usage count and the port autosuspends (100 ms) → `_PS3` cuts power → `__pci_bus_set_current_state` marks the GPU D3cold. The end state is consistent and genuinely off, but "not powered up to wake" in SPEC item 3 is not literally true and the measured resume gain is only the skipped RM resume. No fix inside the nvidia driver; document it, and keep W1's re-save (finding 5).

**4. MEDIUM — stock path with `DPM_FLAG_MAY_SKIP_RESUME` is safe only because the GPU has wakeup capable-but-disabled.** `patches/nvsleep/nvsleep-610.57.04.patch:203`, `drivers_pci_pci-driver.c:970`, `drivers_base_power_main.c:1491`.
On the busy/stock path the GPU is active with RM suspended. `must_resume` is forced only by `pci_pm_suspend_noirq` line 970 (`device_can_wakeup && !device_may_wakeup`) or by `pm_runtime_need_not_resume` being false. If anyone enables `power/wakeup` on 01:00.0, and the audio drops its supplier ref before late (autosuspend inside a slow `dpm_suspend`) and RM holds no ref, `usage_count<=1` → `must_resume=false` → `device_resume_noirq` calls `pm_runtime_set_suspended` on an RM-active GPU in D3hot; `pci_pm_resume` powers it up and `nvidia_resume` runs, but runtime status says "suspended": the card never runtime-suspends again and the next `rpm_resume` runs `rm_transition_dynamic_power(exit)` on an active GPU. Fix (2 lines): in the stock branch of `nv_pmops_suspend_late` set `dev->power.may_skip_resume = false;` (the same thing pci-driver.c:971 does), or `pm_runtime_get_noresume` in the stock `nv_pmops_suspend` and `put` in `nv_pmops_resume`.

**5. Confirmed correct (no change): W1's stock-path changes.**
- `nv_pmops_suspend` resuming a runtime-suspended card (`patch:150-154`): equivalent to what `pci_pm_suspend:845` did before SMART_SUSPEND; `prev` is captured before the callback so the "state not saved" WARN cannot fire.
- `.suspend_late` is only reached on the stock path or on the raced-awake path (`pci_pm_suspend_late:873` skips it when still suspended); -EBUSY there is handled: `device_suspend_late:1689` re-enables runtime PM, `dpm_resume` runs `pci_pm_resume`, and `nv_pmops_resume` correctly does nothing.
- The re-save in `nv_pmops_resume` (`patch:183-184`) is required: `pci_restore_standard_config` consumes `state_saved`; without the re-save the next runtime resume after the port's `_PS3` would restore nothing and RM would touch unprogrammed BARs. The `current_state == PCI_D0` guard is right (saving a D3cold device stores ~0).
- Hibernate: `PM_HIBERNATION_PREPARE`/`POST_HIBERNATION` fall through to stock; `pci_pm_freeze:1083` resumes unconditionally regardless of SMART_SUSPEND; `dev_pm_skip_resume` returns false for RESTORE. `poweroff` with a runtime-suspended card is skipped cleanly and `pci_pm_restore_noirq` restores from the runtime-saved state.

**6. Confirmed correct: lock pairing and races.**
PREPARE skip → `down_write(nv_system_pm_lock)` held, state `IN_STANDBY`; POST (also delivered after an abort via `pm_notifier_call_chain_robust`) → syscore cleared on every sibling, lock released, state `RUNNING`. `nv_sleep_skip_end` ignores `nv_sleep_skip_idle`, so toggling between PREPARE and POST is safe; param 0 never touches `nv_sleep_skipping`. Card woken before `dpm_suspend`: `pm_runtime_barrier` (`main.c:1894`) executes any pending request, `pci_dev_need_resume` is true, `nv_pmops_suspend` returns -EBUSY, `is_suspended` stays false so no resume callback runs. Audio woken: it cannot resume without `rpm_get_suppliers` waking the GPU, so the same abort. Woken between suspend and late: `__pm_runtime_disable(check_resume=true)` runs it synchronously, late returns -EBUSY. Syscore on the audio: prepare `get_noresume` / complete `put`, late `pm_runtime_disable` / early `pm_runtime_enable` all pair (`main.c:2137/1247`, `1654/947`). `pci_dev_put(NULL)` is safe, refs balanced. No deadlock: `nv_pmops_runtime_resume` does not take `nv_system_pm_lock` (stock already runtime-resumes under the write lock, trace line 16-48).

**7. LOW — three nits.**
- `patch:147` stock `pm_runtime_resume` error is ignored (same as the old core behaviour).
- `patch:186` prints "GPU left off, skipping resume" also on the raced-awake abort unwind; misleading log only.
- With nvidia loaded but `nv_linux_devices` empty, `nv_sleep_walk_devices(-1)` returns idle and counts a skip; harmless.
- `patch:168`: after `dpm_suspend_late` runtime PM is disabled, so an RM entry from a kernel thread (not an ioctl, those block on the lock) would get a silent `-EACCES` from `nv_indicate_not_idle` and run on a dead card. Processes are frozen by then; low likelihood, no cheap fix.

**8. LOW — script.** `scripts/luminos-nvidia-defer:128`: when nvsleep fails after a clean dry-run the script exits 1 without rebuilding, leaving a freshly nvdefer-patched source with a stale module until the next run (fix: `dkms_rebuild; initramfs` before `exit 1`). Everything else checks out: idempotent markers per patch, orig copies taken after nvdefer so `restore_orig nvsleep nvdefer` ends at pristine, dkms failure restores both, rc=2 still builds nvdefer-only and rebuilds the initramfs, trusted source is root-owned/not world-writable, 190 lines ≤ 200.

**Not verified.** The patched tree has zero `.o` files and no build log, so "compiles with zero new warnings" is unproven; `tests/nvsleep/static.sh` could not be run in this session (needs approval). Syntax looks right by inspection (static prototype + non-static definition matches the existing `nv_pmops_suspend` pattern, `dev_pm_syscore_device` is GPL-exported and the module is dual MIT/GPL). Patch budget by hand count: 144 added lines, longest function 25 lines, nesting 3.

VERDICT: not safe to install — the patch itself is sound, but installed with contract §D as written it cannot work (finding 1), and the acceptance test will fail a correct run (finding 2). Drop 00:01.1 from the wake policy, fix the rpm_resume count, add the two-line `may_skip_resume` guard (finding 4), compile once, then it is safe.
